title: Why a Perfect Explanation Can Make You More Wrong
question: Why a Perfect Explanation Can Make You More Wrong
hook: An AI's explanation of its cancer prediction was completely accurate — and it made the radiologist MORE confident in a wrong call.
core_idea: Post-hoc explanations faithfully describe the model's internal accounting — including its learned shortcuts — so a correct explanation of a wrong model transfers unearned confidence to the human reading it.
visual_object: a confidence meter attached to a two-path decision (prediction alone vs prediction + explanation)
exclusions: no SHAP math, no Shapley axioms, no Pearl-ladder terminology, no Wittgenstein; keep the radiologist case labeled as a composite (the book flags it)
